entries.citation: E. Bedford and B. A. Taylor, The Dirichlet problem for a complex Monge-Ampere equation, Invent. Math. 37 (1976), 1--44; A new capacity for plurisubharmonic functions, Acta Math. 149 (1982), 1--40.
units: bounded local product and comparison/Dirichlet uniqueness theory
entries.statement: Locally bounded psh potentials have closed positive mixed Bedford-Taylor products, continuous under local uniform approximation. On a finite compact-Kahler time annulus, a bounded total psh potential with zero homogeneous MA measure and prescribed boundary values is the weak geodesic, by the comparison principle.
entries.application: Only bounded finite-time cylinder potentials, explicit homogeneous solutions and product Perron competitors are used in Sections 3--5. No global ray compactness or unbounded MA comparison is inferred.
entries.proof_check: The bounded product definition and uniform-continuity proof are inspected through Demailly's primary text, Chapter III Section 3; comparison/Dirichlet uniqueness is an imported classical foundation. The C1,1 determinant identification is reconstructed in Section 1 by convolution, uniform Hessian bounds, almost-everywhere convergence and BT continuity.
entries.status: standard foundational import; no claimed independent reproof of the entire BT theory

entries.citation: J.-P. Demailly, Complex Analytic and Differential Geometry, version 21 June 2012.
entries.version: 21 June 2012, as printed on primary-text title page
units: Chapter I Theorem 5.24, with complete preceding polar-set proof
Chapter III Section 8, Proposition 8.16 preceding the decomposition formula, and complete subtraction/decomposition proofs
entries.statement: If A is a closed pluripolar subset of a complex manifold, a psh function on its complement locally bounded above near A extends uniquely psh. If T is a closed positive current of bidimension (p,p) and A an irreducible p-dimensional analytic subset, its restriction to A is m_A[A], where m_A is its generic Lelong number; in particular T-m_A[A] is positive.
entries.application: For total rays, add a smooth local background potential; the central divisor is closed pluripolar by log|f| and the total potential is bounded above. On a smooth modification use p=N-1, T a closed positive (1,1) current and A a prime divisor. The remaining current has a local psh potential, which is bounded above and gives the needed logarithmic upper bound.
entries.transport: Demailly uses logarithmic weights; the paper's squared-log potential has the same divisor coefficient after scaling its potential. Poincare-Lelong is explicitly fixed, so the transverse nonintegrability exponent is -2*b*lambda+2*k.
entries.proof_check: Inspected browser lines 3213--3228 and 13794--13900. These local proofs invoke the classical positivity and Lelong-set foundations. The author's two hosting endpoints timed out; the dated primary mathematical text was read at its public Harvard mirror.

entries.citation: T. Darvas, The Mabuchi geometry of finite energy classes, Adv. Math. 285 (2015), 182--219.
entries.statement: On E1, d1(u,v)=E(u)+E(v)-2E(P(u,v)). There is a constant C depending only on dimension such that C^-1 I1(u,v)<=d1(u,v)<=C I1(u,v), where I1 is the sum of the integrals of |u-v| against the two normalized MA measures.
entries.application: All start and fixed-time potentials are E1 on a fixed connected compact smooth Kahler manifold. For u<=v the rooftop is u and the ordered metric identity follows. If w_j converges d1 to w, the supporting energy inequality plus I1 comparison proves E(max(w_j,w))->E(w), used in Theorem 8.2.
entries.transport: Source potential scale is i partial barpartial. Multiply its potentials and its energy/d1 by 2*pi to use the paper's convention. MA probability stays the same.
entries.proof_check: Full Theorem 5.5 proof, browser lines 2830--2972, and Corollary 4.14 inspected. No equality between an NA roof metric and the ray metric is used.

entries.citation: R. J. Berman, T. Darvas and C. H. Lu, Convexity of the extended K-energy and the large time behaviour of the weak Calabi flow.
entries.statement: For p>=1, a potential in E^p and an usc f with e^-f in L1(omega^n), there are smooth Kahler potentials converging in d_p and with the corresponding twisted entropy converging. On a compact connected Kahler manifold the Chen-Tian formula defines the greatest d_p-lower-semicontinuous extension of K-energy, convex along E^p finite-energy geodesics. The energy terms in that formula have d1-continuous extensions; normalized AM energy is affine along finite-energy geodesics.
entries.application: Use p=1, f=0 and untwisted K-energy. The smooth approximation of a finite-entropy starting potential has finite convergent M_C constants. At a fixed time apply d1 lower semicontinuity before the time limit. The results impose no integral-class condition.
entries.transport: q=u/(2*pi) has the same current. Ric_BDL=2*pi Ric_C, E_BDL=E_C/(2*pi), d1_BDL=d1_C/(2*pi), and the contracted terms give M_C exactly; probability entropy is unchanged.
entries.proof_check: Complete pertinent entropy-approximation and lsc/convexity proof units inspected, including the Monge-Ampere density truncation and finite-time geodesic approximation. Their MA solvability and earlier finite-energy metric foundations remain imports.
entries.status: applicable analytic input; no arbitrary strong entropy continuity asserted

entries.citation: P. Mesquita--Piccione and D. Witt Nystrom, A transcendental non-Archimedean Calabi-Yau theorem with applications to the cscK problem.
entries.statement: For a fixed smooth compact Kahler X, class alpha and a PL obstacle f_D>=1 on a smooth dominating SNC model, Gamma=A+D is big, and phi=P_alpha(f_D) has model MA probability V^-1 sum b_i <Gamma^n>.E_i delta_v_i. Its NA entropy is V^-1 <Gamma^n>.(K_relative+B_red-B), and its normalized NA energy is Vol(Gamma)/((n+1)V). The source also gives mixed positive-product intersections.
entries.application: Sections 7 and 8 use the genuine fixed-X analytic NA theory. Central translations are stated and undone. All models in NA applications are C*-equivariant. The entropy coefficient follows independently by summing b_i A_X(v_i)=a_i+1-b_i.
entries.proof_check: Complete supplied units 02 and 04 and public proof units inspected. The source identifies increasing continuous-envelope approximants with restricted positive products and proves the total mass equals V. Its continuity/envelope/orthogonality foundations are imported.
entries.status: external NA model formulas used within their precise obstacle scope

units: Theorem B, Theorem 8.2.1 and constructive proof of Theorem 9.2.1
entries.statement: On E1 NA the strong topology has quasi-metric J(phi,psi)+|sup phi-sup psi|. Weak divisorial convergence with bounded J implies L1 convergence against each fixed MA output of a finite-energy potential. Every finite-energy measure is recovered strongly with entropy convergence by measures supported on dual complexes. The NA MA homeomorphism and continuity theorem solve these measures, and subdivisions of the same complex permit uniform PL-obstacle approximation with entropy convergence.
entries.application: Ordered NA energy convergence gives vanishing J, then strong convergence after removal/restoration of suprema. The fixed-output result is used to estimate E(max(eta_j,phi))-E(phi), not entropy continuity. Two-stage obstacle recovery is kept separate from relatively Kahler model recovery.
entries.proof_check: Complete pertinent supplied units 02--04 and public proof units inspected. The paper reconstructs fixed-output integration and corrects the last scalar identity to |a-b|=2(max(a,b)-b)-(a-b). MA homeomorphism is an external foundational theorem, not independently reproved.
entries.status: applicable strong-theory input; final special-model recovery conditional

entries.citation: A. Trusiani, On the transcendental Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture.
units: complete Theorem B proof and Section 5 vertical-equivariant construction
entries.statement: For a big class gamma on a smooth compact Kahler N-fold, the preprint asserts Kahler Fujita data p_k:Y_k->X, effective E_k, beta_k=p_k^*gamma-E_k Kahler, beta_k^N->Vol(gamma), and beta_k^(N-1).K_Yk-><gamma^(N-1)>.K_X. Lemma 3.4 characterizes specialness by beta_k^(N-1).K_Yk/X->0. Lemma 3.5 gives convergence of fixed mixed non-pluripolar masses. Section 5 asserts vertical invariant centers/defects for the big test-configuration application.
entries.application: The intended application has N=n+1, smooth SNC dominating test space, big Gamma translated to f_D>=1, non-Kahler locus central. It would supply all three hypotheses of Theorem 7.1. Theorem A's automorphism restriction is not imposed on B, and A's stability implication is not used.
entries.proof_check: Full pertinent proofs inspected, rather than inferred from the title or abstract. Proposition 4.1 imports the companion analytic proof; its false normal-differential step is exhibited by Proposition 10.1. The stated theorem is not refuted, but this supporting chain is not independently validated here.
entries.status: unresolved source application; not an unconditional theorem granted to this paper

entries.citation: A. Trusiani, A solution to the Yau-Tian-Donaldson conjecture through special Fujita approximations, with Appendix A by S. Boucksom.
units: Appendix A Proposition A.1 and full proof
entries.statement: For an ideal I on a smooth N-fold and a Rees prime on its normalized blow-up, the asserted discrepancy estimate is ord_F K<=N(ord_F I-ord_F J(I)). The analytic proof claims the residual form can be made Kahler in the normal direction by increasing the pulled-back background form. The algebraic appendix instead uses relative Nadel vanishing and multiplier-ideal subadditivity to generate the required sheaf at a generic Rees divisor.
entries.application: The analytic proof is the exact supporting unit invoked by T26 Proposition 4.1. The algebraic appendix has smooth algebraic characteristic-zero hypotheses. No automatic extension to all analytic ideals on compact Kahler manifolds is made.
entries.proof_check: Analytic proof browser lines 717--1039 and appendix lines 1527--1580 inspected. The false assertion is at lines 749--758; the determinant cancellation follows at 823--832. The explicit normalized blow-up (x^2,y^3) has x=w^3 v,y=w^2 v, dp=0 at w=0, ideal order 6 and Jacobian w^4 v. Its residual form has no normal component for any added C rho^*omega.
entries.status: proof-step counterexample; no counterexample to the discrepancy theorem or known projective results

entries.citation: S. Boucksom, T. Hisamoto and M. Jonsson, Uniform K-stability, Duistermaat-Heckman measures and singularities of pairs: the differential-geometric aspects.
units: Lemma 3.11 and local SNC integral proof
entries.statement: In logarithmic metric weight convention, cohomological Ricci uses half the dd_L log-volume, entropy in the cohomological Mabuchi formula is half probability entropy, and induced volume is exp(2*Psi). On an SNC degeneration the relevant log-volume integral has polynomial growth in log time, hence logarithmic error o(t).
entries.application: Sections 2 and 9 explicitly transport exponents. Our squared-log weight F has divisor coefficients c_i=a_i+1-b_i, so exp(F) times pullback volume has factors |z_i|^(2(b_i-1)); the local simplex computation proves a polynomial bound retaining every b_i.
entries.proof_check: Pertinent convention and local proof inspected; the paper supplies its own general-multiplicity calculation. This is not a hybrid compactness theorem.
entries.status: normalization comparison and local integrability only

entries.citation: P. Mesquita--Piccione, A non-Archimedean theory of complex spaces and the cscK problem.
entries.statement: In its compact-Kahler NA theory, psh functions are determined by divisorial values, rays have the ordinary total-ray datum, and each E1 start with each E1 NA datum has a unique actual maximal ray. It prints affine/mixed slope identities, the maximal-ray entropy lower bound and the finite-Mabuchi-slope maximality transfer from Li.
